options.text: A cell found only in plants
A cell that has already differentiated into a specific type
An undifferentiated cell that can divide and develop into different cell types
A dead cell that provides structural support

questions.explanation: A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell capable of dividing by mitosis and differentiating into specialised cell types. They serve as an internal repair system.

questions.stem: Which type of stem cell can differentiate into any cell type in the body?

options.text: Embryonic stem cells
Meristematic cells
Adult stem cells
Red blood cells

questions.explanation: Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent, meaning they can differentiate into almost any cell type in the body. This makes them particularly valuable for medical research.

questions.stem: Where are adult stem cells found in the human body?

options.text: Only in the embryo
In every cell of the body
In the bone marrow and some other tissues
Only in the brain

questions.explanation: Adult stem cells are found in specific locations such as bone marrow, where they can produce blood cells, and in some other tissues. They are more limited in what they can become compared to embryonic stem cells.

questions.stem: What is one potential medical use of stem cells?

options.text: Replacing faulty genes in DNA
Increasing a person's height
Making antibiotics
Treating conditions like paralysis by replacing damaged nerve cells

questions.explanation: Stem cells have the potential to treat conditions such as paralysis, diabetes, and heart disease by replacing damaged or diseased cells with healthy new ones.

questions.stem: Why are plant stem cells (meristem cells) important in agriculture?

options.text: They prevent pests
They can be used to produce large numbers of identical plants quickly
They provide food for animals
They increase soil fertility

questions.explanation: Meristem cells can be used in tissue culture to produce many genetically identical clones of plants with desirable characteristics, which is valuable in agriculture and horticulture.

questions.stem: What is a major ethical concern about using embryonic stem cells?

options.text: They come from early embryos, which raises moral questions about the status of the embryo
They always cause cancer
They can only be taken from animals
They are too expensive to use

questions.explanation: The use of embryonic stem cells is controversial because extracting them involves destroying the early embryo, which raises ethical questions about when life begins and the rights of the embryo.

questions.stem: How do adult stem cells differ from embryonic stem cells?

options.text: There is no difference between them
Adult stem cells can only differentiate into a limited range of cell types
Adult stem cells are found in embryos
Adult stem cells can become any cell type but embryonic cannot

questions.explanation: Adult stem cells are multipotent, meaning they can only differentiate into a limited range of cell types related to the tissue where they are found. Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent and can become almost any cell type.
